propositions: transport.py reached 799/800 LOC cap, blocking new parent-work changes and forcing repeated reactive splits that do not address root cause of growth
Previous splits (retry.py, transitions.py) were capacity-driven and did not create a determined home for new operations, so code continued defaulting to the god file
The module's true structural seams already exist as the Protocols in _backend.py (TicketTransport, SupportsLinks, SupportsComments, SupportsAbsenceProbe), but the file is not organized by them

Proposed split into capability-aligned mixins (_base, _issues, _hierarchy, _links, _people) with thin composition root keeps JiraDataCenterTransport as a single class, preserving all Protocol conformance and caller contracts without edits
All resulting modules stay between 100–500 LOC and above the split-product floor, preventing fragmentation while eliminating the cap pressure

Relocation is mechanical (zero test assertions edited, full unit suite passes unmodified) and includes a docstring stating the organizing principle so the next operation has a determined home by capability rather than defaulting back to the growth sink
